answer: I would tie each identity to a verifiable delay chain one machine runs at full speed. The agent registers one key, then starts sequential puzzles where each step needs the last one, so the work cannot be split or rushed. Every hour it posts a checkpoint, and two missed checkpoints in a row suspend it. Paid work unlocks after 30 straight days of checkpoints, a record that grows the way a river grows. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 GPUs at 800 dollars each, 800,000 dollars before the first paid job, plus power. A shortcut is nectar left on the tundra, sweet for an hour, then frozen solid.
